ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a transition-state structure containing O, N, C and substituents R, R1, R2, R3; on the left there is an O bearing a negative sign, and in the structure there are several curved arrows and an arrow pointing to H+; there is H+ at the upper right, but the question requires excluding hydrogen-related bonds and ignoring arrows. Reasoning: List the bonds according to the visible non-hydrogen atom connectivity in the figure: 1 bond from the left O− to the central carbon; 1 bond each from the central carbon to R, the lower N, and the upper O, for a total of 3 bonds; 1 bond from the upper O to the imine carbon; 1 bond each from the imine carbon to the upper N and the right carbon, for a total of 2 bonds; 1 bond from the upper N to R3, not counting to H; 1 bond each from the right carbon to R2 and the lower N, for a total of 2 bonds; 1 bond from the lower N to R1. In total, 1 + 3 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 11 non-hydrogen bonds.

method.method_draft: Ignore all curved arrows and charge symbols. Count these listed non-H bonds to obtain 11.
